answer: Nonce-Bound Work Receipts. Each identity must submit a task whose output includes a fresh server-issued nonce and a slow, serial function of it, verified against a private seed held by the requester. Because the nonce differs per request, prior answers cannot be reused or copied. An attacker must run the full computation per clone, paying CPU time and a dune of idle latency for each. Identities are capped by a rotating onyx quota tied to distinct hardware fingerprints. A meadow of plausible clones collapses when per-clone compute exceeds the value of a single vote.
